day.day_focus: Proverbs 1:1-7 - A wise man will hear and increase in learning

timeless_wisdom.quote_text: Though we cannot think alike, may we not love alike?

timeless_wisdom.author: John Wesley

scripture.text:
The proverbs of Solomon the son of David, king of Israel:
To know wisdom and instruction,
To discern the sayings of understanding,
To receive instruction in wise behavior,
Righteousness, justice and equity;
To give prudence to the naive,
To the youth knowledge and discretion,
A wise man will hear and increase in learning,
And a man of understanding will acquire wise counsel,
To understand a proverb and a figure,
The words of the wise and their riddles.
The fear of the Lord is the beginning of knowledge;
Fools despise wisdom and instruction.

exposition.text: Proverbs 1:1-7 opens with a scene marked by wisdom begins with reverent teachability before the Lord. The text does not ask the reader to admire the moment from a distance. The passage puts one clear scene in front of us: A wise man will hear and increase in learning. We should stay with that scene before we rush to a slogan. The literary shape of the passage helps determine the kind of obedience it requires. That keeps the reading honest. The wider context matters too. Proverbs 1:1-7 belongs to a larger movement in which God's wisdom, permission, and worth are being tested under pressure. So the burden here is wisdom begins with reverent teachability before the Lord. The theological lane is true wisdom starts in reverent submission to the Lord rather than self-assured cleverness. The passage stays concrete through The proverbs of Solomon the son of and wise, man, will. What we see in Proverbs 1:1-7 shows how faith responds when suffering, loss, and accusation make reverence costly. The point is not bare information. It presses into faithful response instead of vague admiration. We should not drift into generic encouragement detached from the scene. We should let the passage name the pressure point for the day. If the scene is shaped by A wise man will hear and increase in learning, then obedience today should answer that same pressure point. Where the text exposes fear, we should answer the word with concrete obedience. Where it honors devotion, we should practice humble teachability that receives wisdom as the Lord's gift rather than personal possession. Where it reveals God's worth clearly, we should pursue steady trust in the ordinary places of life rather than delay. That keeps the day under the authority of Scripture. Strong exposition stays close to the text. It does not chase a clever slogan. It lets the details do their work on the conscience. That kind of reading slows us down. It teaches us to listen before we react. It also keeps prayer and application from drifting away from the passage. When the text warns, we should feel the warning. When the text comforts, we should receive the comfort. When the text humbles us, we should not dodge that weight. This is how devotion stays truthful, steady, and alive. The text rewards slow attention because its details are part of its theology, not background decoration. Good application therefore grows from disciplined reading rather than from devotional instinct alone. prompts: Sit with Proverbs 1:1-7 for two quiet minutes. Read the scene of wisdom begins with reverent teachability before the Lord slowly and let it settle before you move on.
Where does this passage call for humble teachability that receives wisdom as the Lord's gift rather than personal possession today?
Stay for one more minute and answer God with one honest sentence of trust, repentance, or gratitude before continuing.

items: Write one sentence naming how Proverbs 1:1-7 presses on the scene of A wise man will hear and increase in learning.
Name one place where humble teachability that receives wisdom as the Lord's gift rather than personal possession should change the way you listen, speak, or act today.

prayer.text: Father, thank You for speaking clearly in Proverbs 1:1-7. In this passage You bring wisdom begins with reverent teachability before the Lord into the open through A wise man will hear and increase in learning. Lord, keep us from reading these words as distant history only, and press them into our ordinary obedience today. Where we resist the truth highlighted in this reflection, bring repentance and renewed trust. Keep us near Your word, and do not let ordinary pressure turn us away from humble obedience. Holy Spirit, take what we have seen in the exposition and turn it into worship instead of mere information. Teach us to remember that Proverbs 1:1-7 opens with a scene marked by wisdom begins with reverent teachability before the Lord. Guard our speech from haste, our work from pride, and our choices from whatever would pull us away from faithful response instead of vague admiration. Help us practice the obedience this day requires with humility as we pursue humble teachability that receives wisdom as the Lord's gift rather than personal possession. Amen.
